label: Lactic-set cheese
step: set slowly with acid, ladle unpressed

about.text: Cheese whose milk is set mainly by lactic acid after a day or more at cool room temperature, with only a trace of rennet; the curd is ladled into moulds, drains by itself and is often ash-coated and mould-ripened for a few weeks.

links.name: Sainte-Maure de Touraine AOP cahier des charges (INAO)

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.
Mostly French goat’s cheeses: a few hundred thousand tonnes of cheese, at about 6 kg of milk a kilo. My own rough estimate.

how.text: The milk is soured for a day or more at cool room temperature with only a few drops of rennet, so the gel is fragile and is ladled into moulds, where it drains under its own weight. Moulds and yeasts then grow on the salted, ash-coated surface.

steps.note: Only a little rennet is added, at most 5 ml of 520 mg/L chymosin per 100 L.

steps.name: ladle
steps.note: By hand into perforated truncated moulds in several passes, no pressing.
Dry salt and charcoal ash on the surface.
In a humid cellar; Valençay is matured at 80 % RH for several weeks (Guelph).

processing.text: Soured by the natural flora of the raw milk and cheese-dairy whey (heterofermentative), or by a lactic starter. Moulds and Candida yeasts on the surface come from the milk, the whey or bought cultures.
